syllabus.text:
Grade-2
PHARMACEUTICS :- Introduction to different dosage forms, their classification with examples—their relative applications.
Familiarization with new drug delivery systems. Introduction to Pharmacopoeias with special reference to the Indian Pharmacopoeia.
Size reduction, Size separation, Metrology—system of weights and measures. Calculations including conversion from one to another
system. Percentage calculations and adjustment of products. Use of alligation method in calculations. Isotonic solutions. Mixing and
homogenization. Packaging of pharmaceuticals Extraction and galenicals, Clarification and filtration, Heat processes, Introduction to
drying processes, Distillation, Sterilization—concept of sterilization and its differences from disinfection—thermal resistance of
microorganisms. Detailed study different sterilization processes. Study of immunological products like sera, vaccines, toxoids and their
preparations., Processing of tablets, Processing of capsules
PHARMACEUTICAL CHEMISTRY :- Acids, bases and buffers, Gastrointestinal agents, Acidifying agents, Antacids, Protectives and
adsorbents, Saline cathartics. Antioxidants, Topical agents — (i) Protectives (ii) Antimicrobials and astringents (iii) Sulphur and its
compounds (iv) Astringents—alum and zinc sulphate. Dental product, Inhalants, Respiratory stimulants, Expectorants and emetics,
Antidotes. Major intra and extracellular electrolytes, Inorganic official compounds of iron, iodine and calcium; ferrous sulfate and
calcium gluconate. Radio pharmaceuticals and contrast media radioactivity, Identification tests for cations and anions as per Indian
Pharmacopoeia. Quality control of drugs and pharmaceuticals
PHARMACOGNOSY :- Definition, history and scope of pharmacognosy including indigenous system of medicine. Various systems of
classification of drugs of natural origin. Adulteration and drug evaluation; significance of pharmacopoeial standards. therapeutic effects
and pharmaceutical applications of alkaloids, terpenoids, glycosides, volatile oils, tannins and resins. Occurrence, distribution,
organoleptic evaluation, chemical constituents including tests wherever applicable and therapeutic efficacy of (a) Laxatives (b)
Cardiotonics (c) Carminatives & G.I. regulators catechu. hyoscyamus, belladonna, aconite, ashwagandha, ephedra, opium, cannabis,
nux vomica. rauwolfia. vasaka, tolu balsam, tulsi. guggal, colchicum, vinca. chaulmoogra oil. pterocarpus, gymnema sylvestro. gokhru,
punarnava. ipecacuanha. benzoin, myrrh, neem, curcuma. cinchona. ergot. shark liver oil and amla. papaya, diastase, yeast. Collection
and preparation of crude drugs from the market as exemplified by ergot, opium, rauwolfia, digitalis, senna. Study of source, preparation
and identification of fibres used in sutures and surgical dressings—cotton, silk, wool and regenerated fibres.
BIOCHEMISTRY AND CLINICAL PATHOLOGY :- Introduction to biochemistry. Brief chemistry and role of carbohydrates, proteins ,
lipids, their classification and related diseases. Role of minerals and water in life processes. Brief chemistry and role of vitamins and
coenzymes. brief concept of enzymatic, Introduction to pathology of blood and urine.
HUMAN ANATOMY AND PHYSIOLOGY :- Definition of various terms used in anatomy, physiology, Structure of cell, unction of its
components with special reference to mitochondria and microsomes. Elementary tissues of the body, Composition of blood, blood
group and coagulation of blood, Name and functions of lymph glands. Anatomy and physiology of different body systems in Brief .
HEALTH EDUCATION & COMMUNITY PHARMACY :- Concept of health—definition, indicators of health, concept of disease,
prevention of diseases. Environment and health. First aid—emergency treatment in shock, snake bite, burns, poisoning, heart disease,
fractures and resuscitation methods. Elements of minor surgery and dressings. Fundamental principles of microbiology, organisms of
common diseases. Non-communicable diseases—causative agents, prevention, care and control. Cancer, diabetes, blindness,
cardiovascular diseases. Communicable disease—causative agents, modes of transmission and prevention. (a) Respiratory
infections—chicken pox, measles, influenza, diptheria, whooping cough and tuberculosis. (b) Intestinal infections—poliomyelitis,
hepatitis, cholera, typhoid, food poisoning, hookworm infection. (c) Arthropod borne infections—plague, malaria, filariasis. (d) Surface
infections—rabies, trachoma, tetanus, leprosy. (e) Sexually transmitted diseases—syphilis, gonorrhoea, AIDS. Nutrition and health,
vitamins and minerals. Demography and family planning, natural family planning methods, chemical methods, mechanical methods,
hormonal, contraceptives, population problem of India. Epidemiology —I mmunity and immunisation, immunological products and their
dose schedule. Principles of disease control and prevention, hospital acquired infection, prevention and control.
DISPENSING PHARMACY :- Prescriptions : Reading and understanding of prescription; Incompatibilities in prescriptions, Posology:
Dose and dosage of drugs, Dispensed Medications: (i) Powders (ii) Liquid oral dosage (b) Biphasic liquid dosage forms: •
Suspensions • Emulsions (iii) Dental and cosmetic preparations: (iv) Semi-solid dosage forms: (a) Ointments (iv) emulsification. (v)
Sterile dosage forms: (a) Parenteral dosage forms (b) Sterility testing, (c) Ophthalmic products— study of essential characteristics of
different ophthalmic preparations.
PHARMACEUTICAL CHEMISTRY II :- chemistry of pharmaceutical organic compounds covering their nomenclature, chemical
structure, uses and the important physical and chemical properties. The stability and storage conditions and the different types of
pharmaceutical formulations of the drugs.
Pharmacology and Toxicology :- Introduction to pharmacology, scope of pharmacology. Routes of administration of drugs, their
advantages and disadvantages. Various processes of absorption of drugs and the factors affecting them. Metabolism, distribution and
excretion of drugs. General mechanism of drugs action and the factors which modify drugs action. Pharmacological classification of
drugs. (i) Drugs acting on the central nervous system: (a) General anaesthetics, intravenous anesthetics. (b) Analgesic, antipyritic,
sedatives and hypnotics, anti-convulsants, (ii) Local anaesthetics. (iii) Drugs acting on autonomic nervous system. (iv) Drugs acting one
eye, (v) Drugs acting on respiratory system (vi) Antacids, (vii) Cardiovascular drugs, (viii) Drugs acting on the blood and blood forming
organs. (ix) Drugs affecting renal function (x) Hormones and hormone antagonists (xi) Drugs acting on digestive system
Pharmaceutical Jurisprudence
--------

syllabus.part: Technical Trade Based Syllabus (SYLLABUS) | Paper Code G | Post Codes: 29, 30, 32, 50, 51, 58
syllabus.subject: (G) Radiographic Technician/Radiographer, Dark Room Assistant, X-Ray Technician
syllabus.text:
Anatomy and Physiology of Human Body
Introduction to the body as a whole. The cells, Tissues, Epithelium: Simple: Compound, Connective Tissues, Muscles, Cell
regeneration, Membranes: mucous, serous, synovial Osteology (including whole skeleton, bones and joints) Development of bone
(osteogenesis): cells involved Types and function of bone, Types of joints and various movement. Axial Skeleton: Skull, Vertebral
Column, Appendicular skeleton, Healing of bones.The respiratory system: Organs, Functions, Pharynx Larynx – Functions, lungs:
lobes, lobules, pleura.
Radiographic, Photography
Photographic process, Photographic emulsions, Film materials in x-ray department. History, structure of an x-ray film, single sided
films, types of films, Spectral sensitivity of film material, graininess of film material, speed and contrast of photographic material,
Sensitometry: photographic density, characteristic curve features of the characteristic curve, The storage of film materials and
radiograph: Storage of unprocessed films, storing of radiographs, Intensifying screens and cassettes. Luminescence: fluorescence and
phosphorescence. Construction of an intensifying screen, The fluorescent materials. Types of intensifying screens. Intensification
factor. The influence of KV, scattered radiation. Detail, sharpness and speed, size of the crystals, reciprocity failure, Cassette design,
care of cassettes, mounting of intensifying screens, Care of intensifying screens, tests to check screen film contact and light leakage,
Film processing: Development: The nature of development, manual, automatic. The PH scale, The constitution of developing solutions
and properties of development chemicals, The development time, factors in the use of a developer. Developers in processing systems,
Film processing: fixing and role of a fixing solution. Constitution of the fixing solutions and properties of the Constituents, Fixers used in
automatic processors. Factors affecting the use of the fixer, Regeneration of fixing solution. Silver recovery and its various methods,
Rinsing, washing and drying. Objects of rinsing and washing, methods employed. Methods of drying films, Preparation of solutions and
making stock solution, Processing equipment: , Dark room: , Systems for daylight film handling , The radiographic image ,
Unsharpness in the radiographic image. Various factors contributing towards unsharpness, The presentation of the Radiograph.
Identification markers and orientation. Documentary preparation, Viewing accessories, Light images and their recording, Fluorography:
, Subtraction: , Common film faults due to manufacturing as well as due to chemical processing, Management of the quality of the
Radiographic image.
ELEMENTARY RADIATION PHYSICS
Structure of matter and principles of machines, electricity and electromagnetism applied in radiological instruments. Physics principles
in design and working of x-ray tube technology. Construction and working principles of transformers and autotransformers used in x-ray
circuits. Measurement of voltage special KV meters. Measurement of tube current in milli and microamperes. Principles of thermionic
emission and rectification in x-ray technology. High voltage D.C. circuits in imaging and therapy tube circuits. Electrical hazards and
safety x-ray tube rating in imaging and therapy x-ray tubes and thermal safety. Introduction to intensity of radiation in general and its
variation by distance. Introduction to eletroma-genetic spectrum, definition of wavelength and its quantum relationship with peak
kilovoltage. Physical principles of radiation and optical field coverage and the factor affecting the field projected on patient during x-ray
imaging and radiotherapy exponential and trigonometric functions used in radiological calculations.
Radiography Techniques
Skeletal system: Radiography techniques for x-ray of: (a) Upper limb with special reference to joint. (b) Lower limb which includes all
the bones with special reference to joint. femur and metatarsals, etc. (c) Shoulder girdle and thorax. (d) Vertebral column with special
techniques for cervical spine, intervertebral joints and formina. Limbo-sacral joint. (e) Pelvic girdle and hip region. (f) Respiratory
system chest radiography for both the lungs, apical, lordotic and oblique views, techniques to decubitus AP and lateral views.
Anatomy and Physiology of Human Body :
Types of cells, tissues, bones and joints. Introduction to system and cavities of the body. Heart and Blood vessels, The Lymphatic
System: The Digestive System:, The Urinary System:, The Reproductive System: Male & Female Reproductive system:, The
Endocrine System:, The Organs of Sense:
RADIATION PHYSICS INCLUDING RADIATION PROTECTION
Atomic structure as applied to generation of x-rays and radioactivity spectrum of diagnostic imaging and therapy x-rays. Effects of
variation of tube voltage, current, filtration, HT waveform and target material on x-ray production. Laws of radioactivity and decay
schemes of different alpha, beta, gamma ray, negatron and position emitters as used in medicine especially in radiotherapy. Artificial
radionuclide generators employed in medicine in general and radiotherapy sources in particular. Interaction of radiation with matter
attenuation absorption and scattering phenomena. Photoelectric absorption, Compton scattering, pair production and annihilation
process, ionisation, effects of geometry of thickness of the absorber. Dependence on the nature and atomic number of the absorber
and on radiation quality. Transmission of x-ray through body tissues. Linear energy transfer. Range of secondary electrons and
electron build up. Relative amounts of scatter from homogeneous and heterogeneous beam during the passage through a patient.
Physical requirements of beam defining devices e.g. cones, diaphragm, collimators etc. Units of radiation measurement specification of
quality and half-valve thickness (HVT) and its measurements, filters and filtration. Measurements of radiation and dosimetric
procedures. Radiation detectors and their principles of working. Definitions of Bragg-peak, percentage depth dose, and peak scatter
factor, tissue air-ratio, tissue maximum ratios scatter air ratio, isodose curves and radiation penumbra of different beams. Wedge filters,
scattering foils. Physics properties of phantoms, phantom materials, bonus and bolus substitutes. Factors used for treatment dose
calculation method. Physical aspects of electron and neutron beam therapy.
Radiation Protection:
Definition of radiation hazards maximum permissible dose and annual limit of intake (ALI), permissible dose levels on and around
sealed source housing and installation principles of radiation protection and MPD’s of different ICRP rules, stochastic and non-
stochastic effects. Importance of ‘ALARA’ physical principles of design and planning of radiation installation. Safe work practice in tele
therapy and Brach therapy. Shielding materials, radiation surveys and personnel monitoring devices film badges. TLD badges, pocket
dosimeters.
BASIC RADIOGRAPHIC TECHNIQUES
Skull: Radiography of cranial bones, cranium, sella turcica, orbit, optic foramina, superior orbital fissure and inferior orbital fissure.
Facial Bones:. Dental Radiography:. Abdomen:, Macro radiography:, Stereography:, Soft tissue techniques: , Operation theatre
techniques:
Radiography:- techniques including special procedures.
Ventriculography and encephalogrphy, Myelography, Angiogrphy

syllabus.part: Technical Trade Based Syllabus (SYLLABUS) | Paper Code L | Post Codes: 40
syllabus.subject: (L) Ayurveda Compounder
syllabus.text:
Ayurveda Compounder -- Syllabus
Introduction to Ayurveda and Health Education
1. Introduction to Ayurveda, its characteristics, the purpose of Ayurveda.
2. Ashtanga Ayurveda (the eight branches of Ayurveda) and the Laghutrayi and Brihattrayi (the lesser and greater triads of classical texts), and the well-known texts of each branch.
3 Definition of a healthy person (Swastha), Trisutra, Chatushpada, Tristambha, Triupastambha (the three aims, four pillars, three supports and three sub-supports of life).
4 General introduction to Dosha, Dhatu, Mala and Agni, their definitions, types and characteristics.
5. Introduction to various scientific terms - Dravya (Sthavara, Jangama, Parthiva), various types of medicine (Daivavyapashraya, Sattvavajaya), aggravation (Prakopa), pacification (Prashamana), the two types of medicine (Shodhana, Shamana), seasons (Ritu), Adana Kala and Visarga Kala, Hansodaka, regions (Jangala, Anupa, Sadharana), general and specific principles (Samanya, Vishesha), the five great elements (Panchamahabhuta), body constitution (Deha Prakriti) and mental constitution (Manasa Prakriti), wholesome and unwholesome (Pathya and Apathya).
6. Time of taking medicine, Anupana (the vehicle/accompaniment taken with medicine) and its importance.
7. Journals and periodicals of Ayurveda.
8. Definition and concept of health.
9. Health and diet.
10. Factors causing the origin of disease (Vyadhi).
11. Swasthavritta (the regimen for maintaining health).
12 Communicable diseases and their prevention.
13. General knowledge of the ideal village, water supply and sanitation.
14. Maternal and child welfare, pre-natal and post-natal care, immunization, family welfare and family planning.
15. Introductory and practical knowledge of muscles and bones. Muscles: Deltoid, Biceps and Triceps. Bones: Femur, Tibia, Fibula, Humerus, Radius, Ulna. Veins: Jugular vein, Femoral vein, Superior Vena Cava, Inferior Vena Cava. Arteries: Radial and Coronary artery.
16. General introduction and knowledge of the respiratory system, circulatory system, digestive/urinary and reproductive systems and the nervous system.
17. General introduction and knowledge of pulse, blood pressure, respiration, respiratory rate, temperature and passing urine through a catheter, and the maintenance of intake and output charts.

Dravyaguna Vigyan (Ayurvedic Pharmacology)
1. General introduction to Dravyaguna and knowledge of the major texts (Nighantus).
2. General introduction to Dravya, Rasa, Guna, Virya, Vipaka and Prabhava.
3 Classification of Dravyas according to the Brihattrayi and according to modern views.
4 The Panchabhautic composition of Dravyas, the six-fold nature of Rasas (Shadvidhatva), the properties and actions of the six Rasas beginning with Madhura (sweet).
5. Preliminary knowledge of the following scientific terms: Deepana, Pachana, Shamana, Anulomana, Sramsana, Bhedana, Rechana, Vamana, Grahi, Stambhana, Chhedana, Lekhana, Vajikarana, Rasayana, Vyavayi, Vikashi, Madakari, Pramathi, Abhishyandi, Yogavahi.
6. Knowledge of the following technical terminology: Dashamula, Panchavalkala, Triphala, Trikatu, Trimada, Trijata, Chaturjata, Panchakola, Chagandhan (?) Trinamula, Kantakapancha, Ashtadugdha, Sneha, Mutra, Chaturamla, Panchamla, Dashemani.
7 Collection of Dravyas according to the seasons, the importance of Dravyas and substitute Dravyas (Pratinidhi Dravya).
8. Methods of collecting Dravyas, extracting medicinal substances from the collected Dravyas and drying them, identifying medicinal Dravyas and methods of separating them from adulterant substances (Updravya).
9. Cultivation of medicinal plants.
10. Introduction, synonyms and medicinal properties and actions of the following Dravyas:
Kantakari, Brihati, Shalaparni, Prishniparni, Gokshura, Patala, Bilva, Agnimantha, Haritaki, Shyonaka, Amalaki, Shunthi, Gambhari, Pippali, Chitraka, Pippalimula, Parasapippala, Vata, Ashvattha, Udumbara, Neem, Plaksha, Tulasi, Kumari, Balachatushtaya, Shatavari, Arjuna, Shankhapushpi, Sharapunkha, Aragvadha, Eranda, Snuhi, Nirgundi, Nimbu, Bhunimba, Bhringaraja, Nagarmotha, Durva, Dhanyaka, Dhataki, Guduchi, Madhuka, Kutaja, Punarnava, Maricha, Shirisha, Apamarga, Arka, Ajamoda, Amlika, Patha, Badara, Madanaphala, Vidanga, Shalmali, Shobhanjana, Shishapa, Kakamachi, Manjishtha, Brahmi, Ela, Katuki, Pashanabheda, Vidari, Chandana, Jatamansi, Dadima, Kushmanda, Vartaka, Karkatashringi, Shatapushpa, Daruharidra, Karavira, Bhumyamalaki, Vijayasara, Ativisha, Paryataka, Priyala, Methika, Kampillaka, Haridra, Sarpagandha, Sarpagandha, Kapittha, Masuli (?), Madhurashti, Mandukaparni, Parasika Yavani, Gorakhmundi, Bakuchi, Ashwagandha, Palasha, Vacha, Mulaka, Vatsanabha, Bakula, Shephalika, Shaiphalika, Lajjalu, Narikela, Bhanga, Pushkaramula, Khadira, Ahiphena, Vasa, Ashoka, Swarnakshiri, Talisapatra, Dhattura, Shimbi, Bhallataka, Lavanga, Tvak, Draksha, Alabu, Shurana, Indrayava, Rasona, Guggulu, Kapikacchu, Kupilu, Kiratika, Jyotishmati, Devadaru, Jatiphala, Dugdhika, Gunja

Rasashastra (Ayurvedic Alchemy and Mineral Pharmaceutics)
1. Introduction to Rasashastra, Rasa and the synonyms of Rasa, the importance of Rasa in Rasashastra, Rasa medicines (Rasaushadhi).
2. Maharasa, Uparasa and Sadharana Rasa, their purification, disorders arising from impure mercury, Dhanyaka (as given).
3. Introduction to metals and Mandura, general and specific methods of purification (Shodhana) of Kharu (?) and Mandura.
4. Introduction and nature of the following Dravyas: Mukta, Pravala, Shankha, Godanti, Badarashma, Samudraphena, Kukkutandatvak, Tankana, Mrigashringa.
5. Introduction and use of the following apparatus (Yantras): Tula, Swatva (?), Ulukhala, Palika, Sthali, Dhola (?), Damaru, Dola (?), Swedani, Vidyadhara, Kachchhapa, various Baluka (sand baths), Patala, Sandhi-vakadamatti (sealing clay).
6. Introduction and use of Puta, general method of use and the use of modern techniques in Putapaka.
7. General knowledge of the following scientific terms: Swangasheeta, Dahisheeta, Dalana, Avapa, Nirvapa, Sattva, Vanaushadhi Sattva, Lavana Panchaka, Kshara Traya, Kshara Panchaka, Panchamrita, Panchagavya, Panchaja, Panchamahisha, Panchamrittika, Kaksas (?), Tanka, Duti, Dravanagana, Dugdhavarga, Gusha (?), Mutravarga, Mudra, Koshthi.
8. Introduction to Shodhana (purification) and its purpose.
9. Introduction to Marana (incineration) and its purpose, Mrita Loha Pariksha (testing of incinerated iron).
10. Acceptable and unacceptable forms of Rasa (mercury), disorders arising from impure mercury and measures for their relief, Rasa Dosha, Rasa Gati, precautions related to the substances and the body during the purification of mercury. General and special methods of purification, general introduction to the eight Samskaras, Hingulottha Parada (mercury from cinnabar) and its importance.
11. Introduction to some formulations of Hingu and Guggulu and their method of preparation.
12. Purification (Shodhana) and Marana procedures of the following Dravyas and introduction to some formulations of each: Pravala, Shankha, Shukti, Kapardika, Sphatika, Dugdhapashana, Godanti, Badarashma, Samudraphena, Kukkutandatvak, Bhringashringa; Shodhana and general uses of Tankana.
13. Pishti Kalpana - introduction, method of preparation, general uses and some formulations of each: Pravala, Muktashukti, Jaharmohra, Akika.
14. Khalviya Rasayana, Kupipakva Rasayana, Parpati Rasayana, Pottali Rasayana.
15. Murchchhana: Sagandha, Nirgandha, Sagni, Niragni, Attadhurma (?), Bala Jarana.
16. Kajjali, Rasaparpati, Panchamrita Parpati, Bola Parpati, Shweta Parpati, Rasa Sindura, Tamra Sindura, Malla Sindura, Samirapannaga, Talastha Swarnabanga, Rasakarpura. Method of preparation and uses of all the above and introduction to some formulations.
17. Description of the Marana of Abhraka, Makshika, Kasisa and Haritala and their general uses, some formulations and Lohitikarana.
18. Description of the Marana, general uses and some formulations of the following substances such as Swarna (gold), Rajata (silver), Loha (iron), Tamra (copper), Mandura, Amritikarana, Bhanupaka, Sthalipaka, Putapaka, description of Somanathi Tamra Bhasma.
19. Jarana and Marana of Naga (lead), Vanga (tin) and Yashada (zinc), general uses of some of their formulations.
20. Introduction, method of preparation and general uses of the following Dravavaka Kalpas: Shankhadrava, Gandhaka Drava.

Bhaishajya Kalpana (Pharmaceutics) and Pharmacy Management
21. Introduction to Bhaishajya Kalpana, the excellent medicine (Prashasta Bhesaja), the importance of medicine among the Chatushpada (four pillars of treatment).
22. Kalpana Samskaras and their shelf life (period of potency), storage and preservation of prepared medicines, taking the meaning in cases of the unstated (Anukta), repetition (Punarukta), Laishakti (?).
23. The importance of measures (Mana), introduction to the various measures and their conversion into the metric system, methods of taking dry and fresh (wet) Dravyas, quantity (Matra) and dose of medicine.
24. Definition of Swarasa (expressed juice), method of preparation, Putapakva Swarasa method, method of preparing Swarasa when fresh Dravyas are not available, general dose, Prakshepa Dravya (added substances), some examples of Swarasa formulations.
25. Definition of Kalka (paste), method of preparation, general dose, Prakshepa and some examples of Kalka formulations.
26. Definition of Kwatha (decoction), method of preparation, general dose, Prakshepa Dravya, Yavakuta and some examples of Kwatha formulations; Pramathya, Aushadha, Sindhu Paniya, Kshirapaka, Laksharasa, Ushnodaka.
27. Definition of Hima (cold infusion), method of preparation, general dose, Prakshepa Dravya, some examples of Hima formulations and Tandulodaka (rice-water).
28. Definition of Phanta (hot infusion), method of preparation, general dose, Prakshepa Dravya and some examples of Phanta formulations.
29. Various Pathya Kalpanas (wholesome preparations) - Manda, Peya, Vilepi, Yavagu, Yusha, Kritakrita, Aushadha-siddha Yusha, Bhakta, Krishara, Mantha, Panaka, Ragashadava, Kambalika Khanda, Mamsa Rasa, Veshavara, Ghola, Mathita, Takra, Udashvit.
30. Nomenclature of medicines.
31. Knowledge of the modern machines used in pharmacy.
A. Cutting/ Chopping Machine. B. Pulveriser. C. Mixer. D. Grinder. E Tablet making Machine. F. Tablet cutting Machine. G Taller Stripes Packing Machine. H. Juice Pressures (Explorer). 1. Pulpar. J. Granulator. K. Furnace. L. Server etc.
32. Introduction to Churna (powders), knowledge of the ancient and modern instruments and equipment used in preparing general therapeutic preparations.
33. Definition of Vatika, Chankeka (?) Vataka and Modaka (pills and sweet balls) and their method of preparation.
34. Guggulu Kalpa - introduction, method of preparation and some of its formulations.
35. Varti Kalpana - introduction to the various Vartis (medicated wicks/suppositories) and their preparation.
36. Avaleha Kalpana - introduction and method of preparation, Guda-Sharkara Paka (jaggery and sugar syrup stages), Paka Pariksha (testing of the syrup stage), Prakshepa Dravya, Ghanasattva and some of its formulations.
37. Khanda Paka - introduction and method of preparation.
38. Kshara Kalpana - introduction and method of preparation, some formulations, method of preparing Kshara Sutra (medicated alkaline thread).
39. Sandhana Kalpana - introduction, Asava and Arishta preparation methods and Sandhi Pariksha (testing of fermentation), Prakshepa and some formulations; introduction to Kanji, its method of preparation and use.
40. Anjana - Trirupa, Rasanjana, Churnanjana and their importance.
41. Introduction to Sneha Kalpana, Sneha Murchchhana, Sneha Paka method, types, purpose and testing.
42. Taila (oils) - Taila, Tilmi (?)
43. Sharkara Kalpana - introduction, method of preparation and Sharkara (syrups).
44. Arka Kalpana - introduction, method of preparation and some examples of Arka, preparation of Netrabindu (eye drops), some formulations.
45. Lavana Kalpana - introduction, method of preparation and some formulations.
46. Masi Kalpana - introduction, method of preparation and some formulations.
47. Introduction and method of preparation of Lepa, Upanaha and Malahara (ointments), and some examples of Pratyarka Kalpana (?).
48. Medicine preservatives, food chemicals and their uses.
49. Knowledge of the major drug stores of India, their maintenance, dispensing and the rules of mixing, knowledge of the symbols used in the prescription.
50. Introductory description of the dispensing of medicine mixtures and the duties of the attendant (Upasthata).
51. Knowledge of medicine dosage according to Ayurveda and modern views.
52. Knowledge of single drugs and mixed drugs and their types.
53. Method of dispensing.
54. Knowledge of the prescription and the maintenance of the dispensing unit by an ideal pharmacist.
55. Technical knowledge of Vrana Nivasanga (?), Chavarga (?), Anjana, Vidalaka and Ashchyotana (eye drops).
56. Sterilization of gauze, bench scissors, knives, forceps, ordinary and dental instruments and knowledge of the use of the instruments in the outpatient hospital (OPD).
57. Business mathematics, statement of income and expenditure, pricing, accountancy and auditing.
58. Brief knowledge of industrial management (promotion) and marketing.
59. Working procedure of the Rasashala (alchemy laboratory), collection, preservation and proper classification of Dravyas, knowledge of medicines.
60. Knowledge of the process of obtaining a drug licence.

syllabus.part: Technical Trade Based Syllabus (SYLLABUS) | Paper Code M | Post Codes: 41
syllabus.subject: (M) Homoeopathy Compounder
syllabus.text:
Homoeopathy Compounder Syllabus
Anatomy:-
1. Origin of normal pregnancy, embryology, development of the body from conception to birth.
2. Limbs and organs of the human body, cells, components, skin, membranes, ligaments, etc.
3. Bones, their number, types, location, teeth, nails, hair, types of joints.
4. Muscles, their number and types.
5. General knowledge of veins, arteries, capillaries, lymph muscles and nodes.
6. Composition of blood, blood pressure and structure of the heart.
7. Description of the respiratory system, larynx, trachea, respiratory tract and lungs.
8. Knowledge of the structure and position of the organs of the digestive system.
9. Brief introduction to the organs of the urinary system.
10. Brief introduction to the reproductive system, the genital organs of men and women, sperm, scrotum, ovum, uterus, ovary, etc.
11. Brief introduction to the joint and ligament system.
12. Brief introduction to the names, position and functions of the ductless glands.
13. Brief introduction to the structure, number, position and functions of the sense organs.
Physiology:-
1. The cell and its types, tissues and organs of the body.
2. Protoplasm, its composition, chemical structure of protein, carbohydrates and enzymes.
3. Physiology of nerves and muscles, types of muscles.
4. Composition of blood, definition, volume, functions of blood, plasma, chemical structure of haemoglobin and its mixture, blood clotting and blood groups.
5. Cardiovascular system - structure and properties of heart muscle, functions of the heart, blood circulation, structure of arteries, veins and capillaries, pulse, blood pressure, etc.
6. Respiratory system - structure and functions of the organs of respiration, respiration - internal and external respiration, etc.
7. Digestive system - digestion of food, functions of the accessory organs, names of the various digestive juices and their actions.
8. Sense organs - sight, hearing, taste, smell, skin.
9. Structure of the kidney - functions, brief introduction, urine, sweat, etc.
10. Reproductive system - brief description of the functions of the male and female reproductive organs.
Homoeopathic Materia Medica and Organon:-
A. Brief introduction to the following homoeopathic medicines, list - 1. Aconite Nap 2. Aethusa Cynapium 3. Aloes 4. Antim Tart 5. Apis Mel 6. Argentum Nitricum 7. Arnica 8. Aurum Met 9. Baptisia 10. Arsenic Alb 11. Baryta Carb 12. Belladonna 13. Bryonia 14. Cactus G 15. Calcarea Carb 16. Cairita (?) 17. Carbo Veg 18. Causticum 19. Chamomilla 20. China 21. Chelidonium 22. Colocynth 23. Conium 24. Cuprum Met 25. Digitalis 26. Ulkamara (?) 27. Ferrum Met 28. Gelsemium 29. Graphites 30. Hamamelis 31. Hepar Sulph 32. Hyoscyamus 33. Ignatia 34. Ipecac 35. Kali Bichrom 36. Kali Carb 37. Lachesis 38. Ledum Pal 39. Lycopodium 40. Merc Sol 41. Natrum Mur 42. Nitric Acid 43. Nux Vomica 44. Phosphorus 45. Podophyllum 46. Pulsatilla 47. Rhus Tox 48. Sepia 49. Sulphur 50. Veratrum Alb
B. List of Biochemic medicines:- 1. Calcarea Fluor 2. Calcarea Phos 3. Calcarea Sulph 4. Ferrum Phos 5. Kali Mur 6. Kali Phos 7. Kali Sulph 8. Mag Phos 9. Natrum Mur 10. Natrum Phos 11. Natrum Sulph 12. Silicea
C. Aphorisms 1 to 70 relating to the principles of homoeopathic treatment
Homoeopathic Pharmacy:-
1. Introduction and the characteristics of homoeopathic pharmacy.
2. Relation of homoeopathic pharmacy with Materia Medica and the national savings (as given).
3. Botanical names, homoeopathic philosophical and chemical systems, measures.
4. Pharmaceutical instruments and equipment related to homoeopathic pharmacology.
5. Sources of homoeopathic medicines - methods of collecting medicinal substances, identification, purification, prevention of spoilage and maintenance of potentised medicines.
6. Medicine and vehicle - their preparation and use, their purification, determining the standard strength of the average.
7. Methods of preparing medicines from organic and inorganic chemicals, animals and animal-derived substances, and disease-derived substances.
8. Methods of preparing mother tinctures, solutions, potentisation and triturations, their purification, determining the standard strength of the spirit (alcohol).
9. Change of potency (Lakshan potency), converting or changing triturations into liquid.
10. Medicines for external use - lotion, liniment, glycerol, ointment or conversion.
11. Treatment sheet (prescription) - its study, satisfactory signs (?), importance, principles and method of writing a prescription.
12. Study of medicines, medicine potency, study of the action of homoeopathic medicines (Pharmacodynamics), potency, speed, dynamic power, knowledge of the dosage of medicine and treatment through it.
13. Brief study of the standard levels of medicinal substances and vehicles.
14. Brief knowledge of general laboratory methods, chemical solutions, mixtures, sedimentation, filtration, crystallisation, sublimation, percolation, etc.
15. Identification, use and methods of cleaning the instruments, equipment and materials used in homoeopathic pharmacy.
16. Identification of some homoeopathic medicinal substances - from the plant family, from the chemical family.
17. Collecting homoeopathic medicines and making a herbarium.
18. Dispensing medicine by reading the patient's treatment sheet and telling the method of taking its dose.
19. Making globules from potentised medicine for its distribution and arranging them at the dispensing counter.
20. Preparing from three mother tinctures up to the 3rd potency.
21. Preparing lotions and liniments for external use.
22. Sublimation, distillation, sterilisation, percolation, etc.
23. A study visit to a homoeopathic laboratory.
Introduction to Maternal and Child Diseases and Treatment:- Maternal and child health, school health fair and health education, etc. Introduction to diseases related to obstetrics and their treatment, paediatric diseases and their treatment. National health problems, urban and backward area health-related problems, their administration and international health relations. Along with family welfare, medicines for disease prevention and immunity, contraceptives, population control, economic aspects related to health and disease, and the environment.
National Health Programmes, Statistics and Maintenance of Registers:- Preventive medicines. Signs of health, social causes of the causes of disease and ill-health, social problems related to the patient, brief description of diseases spreading in the community such as plague, cholera (?), diphtheria, leprosy, tuberculosis, malaria, whooping cough, measles, chickenpox, jaundice, hepatitis, eye diseases, enteric fever (?), dysentery, etc., and measures for their prevention, immunization, etc. Basic elementary knowledge of the principles of health statistics, record keeping.
Emergency Medicine and Personal and Public Hygiene:-
1. Physiological hygiene:- Food and nutritive substances, the balanced basis of food in health and disease, minimum requirement and survey of nutritious diet, food adulteration and its testing, testing of milk and information about diet and preparation, and food poisoning caused by spoiled food. Air, light, sunlight, effect of weather, humidity, temperature and other meteorological conditions and the comfort zone, ill effects of overcrowding. General discussion of teaching related to personal health, cleanliness, rest, sleep, work and physical exercise.
2. Environmental health and sanitation:- Introduction and importance. Environmental pollution, air purification, brief introduction to air-borne diseases. Water supply sources and use, impurities and purification, and public water supply in rural areas. Standards of drinking water, brief introduction to ideal water-borne diseases. Conservatism (orthodoxy), latrines, septic tanks, etc. in use in villages and towns. Arrangement of drains, water and sewage disposal. Sanitation arrangements at festivals and fairs. Deodorants, methods of preventing decay and infection or killing germs, removing germs and disinfection or sterilisation. Insecticides, removal of insects and pests related to diseases, and their control. Brief description of parasitic insects and other diseases and parasites.

syllabus.part: Technical Trade Based Syllabus (SYLLABUS) | Paper Code N | Post Codes: 42
syllabus.subject: (N) Unani Compounder
syllabus.text:
Unani Compounder Syllabus - Basic Introduction to Unani Tibb
Umur-e-Tabiyya (Basic Principles of Medicine):- Definition of Ilm-e-Tibb (the science of medicine), its subject matter, purpose and aim, definition and importance of Tabiyat (temperament/nature). Brief description of Arkan (elements), Mizaj (temperament), Akhlat (humours), Aza (organs), Arwah (spirits), Quwa (faculties), Afal (functions).
Tashreeh-ul-Badan (Anatomy):- Definition, anatomical position, related terminology. Scapula, Clavicle, Humerus, Radius, Ulna, Femur, Tibia. Knee joint, Elbow joint, Hip joint, Shoulder joint. Kibd (liver), Qalb (heart), Riya (lungs), Kulliya (kidneys), Meda (stomach). Basic introduction to the nervous system (Nizam-e-Asab).
Manafe-ul-Aza (Physiology):- Brief description of cells (Khaliya) and tissues (Nasij), components and functions of blood, structure and functions of red blood cells (Kurriyat-e-Humra), blood clotting. Digestive system - saliva (Luab-e-Dahan), gastric secretions (Rutubat-e-Meda), intestinal secretions (Rutubat-e-Amaa), bile (Rabit-e-Safrawiya).
Tahaffuzi wa Samaji Tibb (Preventive and Social Medicine):- Vaccination (National Immunization Schedule), Asbab-e-Sitta Zaruriya (the six essential factors), family planning, WHO, UNICEF, antenatal care.
Ilm-ul-Amraz wa Saririyat (Pathology and Clinical Medicine):- Basic introduction to Ilm-ul-Amraz and Saririyat, inflammation, necrosis, gangrene.

Awhal, Atees, Izkhar, Ajarki, Arusa, Asgandh, Asrol, Amla, Anar, Asl-us-Soos, Babuna, Bawchi, Badiyan, Bihidana, Bahman Surkh, Bahman Safed, Jamun, Zadwar, Chirayata, Khatmi, Khubbazi, Zafran, Zanjabeel, Zeera, Shahtara, Sandal Surkh, Sandal Safed, Karanphal, Aqir Qarha, Mako, Halela Zard, Halela Kabuli, Halela Siyah.

exams.body: मध्यप्रदेश कर्मचारी चयन मण्डल, भोपाल (MP Employees Selection Board, Bhopal)
exams.posts: नर्सिंग ऑफिसर 2099 पद (केवल महिला; पोस्ट कोड 01–11: शासकीय स्वास्थ्य संस्थाएँ 1256 + स्वशासी चिकित्सा महाविद्यालय 843) + सिस्टर ट्यूटर 218 पद (पोस्ट कोड 12, शासकीय नर्सिंग महाविद्यालय) = कुल 2317 पद; तृतीय श्रेणी, अकार्यपालिक
exams.negative: 0.25 mark deducted for each wrong answer
exams.qualifying: UR: 50%; SC/ST/OBC/PwD: 40% (10% relaxation); EWS gets 10% relaxation (selection on merit from EWS list)
rules: Paper

1 paper, 100 marks: (अ) सामान्य ज्ञान, सामान्य हिन्दी, सामान्य अंग्रेजी, सामान्य गणित, सामान्य विज्ञान, सामान्य अभिरुचि – 25 अंक; (ब) संबंधित विषय (B.Sc. Nursing पाठ्यक्रम) पर आधारित प्रश्न – 75 अंक; same paper for both posts; duration 2 hours
Marks per question
प्रत्येक वस्तुनिष्ठ प्रश्न का सही उत्तर अंकित करने पर 1 अंक दिया जायेगा एवं गलत उत्तर अंकित करने पर कुल प्राप्तांक में से प्रत्येक गलत उत्तर के 0.25 अंक घटाए जायेंगे।
Minimum qualifying marks
UR 50%; SC/ST/OBC/नि:शक्तजन 40% (10% छूट); EWS को न्यूनतम अर्ह अंकों में 10% छूट, पर चयन EWS सूची में से मेरिट पर
Language / cancelled questions
Hindi text is standard except science/technical papers (English is standard); marks of a cancelled question are given proportionately to all candidates on marks earned in the paper
Education – Nursing Officer

12th (10+2) with Physics, Chemistry & Biology (PCB); 4-year B.Sc. Nursing, or 2-year Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing after GNM, from an institute recognised by MP Nurses Registration Council / Indian Nursing Council, with at least 45% marks (SC/ST/OBC 5% relaxation); live registration with MP Nurses Registration Council
Education – Sister Tutor
12th (10+2) with PCB; B.Sc. Nursing or Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing pass; experience: B.Sc. (Nursing)/P.B.B.Sc. (Nursing) with 1 year experience; live registration with MP Nurses Registration Council
Age

18–40 yrs; 45 yrs for MP-domicile SC/ST/OBC, govt/corporation/board/autonomous/Home Guard employees, Nagar Sainik, PwD and women; age counted as on 1 Jan 2026; no age relaxation for EWS; absolute max 45 yrs (except contract employees and rule-13 categories); inter-caste marriage awardees & Vikram Award +5 yrs
Other
Nursing Officer posts – women only; live registration at MP Employment Exchange mandatory; selected candidates sign a bond to serve the department at least 5 years (Rs 5 lakh)

en.title: Nursing Officer & Sister Tutor Recruitment 2026
en.name: Nursing Officer & Sister Tutor Recruitment Exam 2026 – Directorate of Public Health & Medical Education, MP
en.body: Madhya Pradesh Employees Selection Board, Bhopal (MP Employees Selection Board, Bhopal)
en.posts: Nursing Officer: 2099 posts (women only; post codes 01–11: Government health institutions 1256 + Autonomous medical colleges 843) + Sister Tutor: 218 posts (post code 12, Government nursing colleges) = total 2317 posts; Class III, non-executive
en.negative: 0.25 mark deducted for each wrong answer
en.qualifying: UR: 50%; SC/ST/OBC/PwD: 40% (10% relaxation); EWS gets 10% relaxation (selection on merit from EWS list)
rules: Paper

1 paper, 100 marks: (A) General Knowledge, General Hindi, General English, General Mathematics, General Science, General Aptitude – 25 marks; (B) Questions based on the relevant subject (B.Sc. Nursing syllabus) – 75 marks; same paper for both posts; duration 2 hours
Marks per question
1 mark will be awarded for marking the correct answer to each objective question, and 0.25 mark will be deducted from the total marks obtained for each wrong answer marked.
Minimum qualifying marks
UR 50%; SC/ST/OBC/PwD (persons with disabilities) 40% (10% relaxation); EWS gets 10% relaxation in minimum qualifying marks, but selection is on merit from the EWS list
Language / cancelled questions
Hindi text is standard except science/technical papers (English is standard); marks of a cancelled question are given proportionately to all candidates on marks earned in the paper
Education – Nursing Officer

12th (10+2) with Physics, Chemistry & Biology (PCB); 4-year B.Sc. Nursing, or 2-year Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing after GNM, from an institute recognised by MP Nurses Registration Council / Indian Nursing Council, with at least 45% marks (SC/ST/OBC 5% relaxation); live registration with MP Nurses Registration Council
Education – Sister Tutor
12th (10+2) with PCB; B.Sc. Nursing or Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing pass; experience: B.Sc. (Nursing)/P.B.B.Sc. (Nursing) with 1 year experience; live registration with MP Nurses Registration Council
Age

18–40 yrs; 45 yrs for MP-domicile SC/ST/OBC, govt/corporation/board/autonomous/Home Guard employees, Nagar Sainik, PwD and women; age counted as on 1 Jan 2026; no age relaxation for EWS; absolute max 45 yrs (except contract employees and rule-13 categories); inter-caste marriage awardees & Vikram Award +5 yrs
Other
Nursing Officer posts – women only; live registration at MP Employment Exchange mandatory; selected candidates sign a bond to serve the department at least 5 years (Rs 5 lakh)

syllabus.text:

and dieing etc.). NOS: ELE/N3114

4. Identify electrical safety. Join different wire, measure power, currents, volts and earth resistance etc. Connect

DOL starter with different types of motors. NOS: ELE/N3112

safety cut out used in sealed compressor. NOS: ELE/N3112
15. Identify the components of control system of Inverter A.C and wiring of control system NOS ELE/N3114
16. Perform servicing & de-scaling of condenser (internals & externals) used in different appliances NOS
ELE/N3114
17. Perform fitting & adjustment of drier, filter & refrigerant controls used in different refrigeration system.
NOS: CSC/N9413
18. Perform servicing of different evaporator used in different appliances. NOS: CSC/N9414
19. Carry out Recovery and Recycling of Refrigerant used, alternative of CFC, HFC re-cover, transfer &

20. Retrofit CFC/HFC machine with ozone friendly refrigerant with understanding of the compatibility. NOS
ELE/N3114
21. Pack thermal insulation and prevent cooling leakage. NOS ELE/N3114
22. Install window AC, test Electrical & electronics components & Fault diagnosis & remedial measures. NOS
ELE/N3114
23. Perform servicing of electrical & electronic control test, installation, wiring, fault finding & remedial
measures of different split AC. NOS ELE/N3114
24. Perform servicing of car AC. Fault diagnosis & remedial measures NOS ELE/N3114
25. Read and apply engineering drawing for different application in the field of work. NOS CSC/N9401
26. Demonstrate basic mathematical concept and principles to perform practical operations. Understand and
explain basic science in the field of study. NOS CSC/N9402
27. Carry out servicing, dismantling, checking different parts of different types of commercial compressor, replacing worn out parts, Check lubrication system. Assemble & check performance. NOS-ELE/N3140
28. Perform servicing of different types of water-cooled condenser. NOS- ELE/N3140
29. Perform servicing and performance test of Cooling tower NOS- ELE/N3141
30. Conduct Servicing, backwash & re-generate Water treatment plant of circulating water. NOS CSC/N9415
31. Perform Fitting of expansion valve, adjustment of refrigerant flow according to heat load. NOS-ELE/N3140
32. Perform servicing of evaporator &chillers. NOS- ELE/N3140
33. Carry out servicing and retrofit of Water cooler and dispenser. NOS CSC/N9416
34. Service, retrofit of visible cooler and bottle cooler and test performance. NOS CSC/N9417
35. Conduct servicing of deep freezer and test performance. NOS CSC/N9418
36. Install, service, repair, gas charging and testing performance of Ice Cube machine. NOS CSC/N9419
37. Repair, servicing & retrofit of ice candy plant. NOS CSC/N9420
38. Perform servicing of Ice plant and evaporative condenser. NOS CSC/N9421
39. Perform Servicing and preventive maintenance of walk in cooler & cold storage. NOS CSC/N9422
40. Study psychrometric chart and measure psychrometric properties using psychrometric, anemometer i.e.
DBT, WBT, RH, air flow etc. NOS-ELE/N3140
41. Perform servicing of motor and blowers used in different air conditioning system. NOS-ELE/N3141
42. Construct, install, pack thermal and acoustic insulation of different air ducts. NOS-ELE/N3141
43. Perform servicing and maintenance of different types of air filters. NOS- ELE/N3141
44. Perform servicing, installation, fault diagnosis and remedial measures on Package AC with Air cooled
condenser. NOS CSC/N9423
45. Carry out Servicing, installation, fault diagnosis and remedial measures in Package A.C. with water cooled
condenser. NOS-ELE/N3140
46. Identify the various components of central AC test electrical components and make wiring. Servicing of
A.H.U, damper, check air flow, De-scaling of condenser and CT servicing. NOS- ELE/N3141
47. Pump down the system, top up oil and gas and check temperature and pressure. NOS-ELE/N3140
48. Identify components of DX system. Test components, make wiring of DX system. Test leak and evacuate,
gas charge the system and check the performance. Maintenance, trouble shoot and operate the plant. NOSELE/N3140
49. Identify the different parts of VRF/VRV system, check and service VRF/VRV system. NOS-ELE/N3141
50. Identify different parts of indirect or chillers system. Check components and make wiring, leak test,
evacuate and gas charge/ top up. Servicing the plant and trouble shoot. NOS-ELE/N3141
51. Identify chilled water pipe line. Servicing of dampers, FCU and water control valves. NOS-ELE/N3141
52. Troubles shoot both Central A.C. plant DX and indirect system. Check different control system, installation
of other major components, servicing of all parts including cooling tower and water treatment plant. NOSELE/N3141
53. Perform Servicing, fault diagnosis, repair and maintenance of mobile A.C. leak test, evacuation, gas
charging, check magnetic clutch and make wiring. Test performance after start. NOS-ELE/N3141
54. Perform preventive maintenance of different plants. Maintain log book based on daily operation. NOSELE/N3141
55. Read and apply engineering drawing for different application in the field of work. NOS CSC/N9401
56. Demonstrate basic mathematical concept and principles to perform practical operations. Understand and
explain basic science in the field of study, NOS CSC/N9402

syllabus.part: ट्रेड पाठ्यक्रम | पेपर कोड 07 | पोस्ट कोड 13 & 14
syllabus.subject: Fitter
syllabus.text:
1. Plan and organize the work to make job as per specification applying different types of basic fitting operation
and Check for dimensional accuracy following safety precautions. [Basic fitting operation - Marking,
Hacksawing, Chiselling, Filing, Drilling, Taping and Grinding etc. Accuracy: ± 0.25mm] CSC/N0304
2. Manufacture simple sheet metal items as per drawing and join them by soldering, brazing and riveting.
CSC/N03001
3. Join metal components by riveting observing standard procedure. CSC/N0304
4. Join metal component by arc welding observing standard procedure. CSC/N0304
5. Cut and join metal component by gas (oxyacetylene) CSC/N0304
6. Produce components by different operations and check accuracy using appropriate measuring instruments.
[Different Operations Drilling, Reaming, Taping, Dieing; Appropriate Measuring Instrument - Vernier, Screw
Gauge, Micrometer] CSC/N0304
7. Make different fit of components for assembling as per required tolerance observing principle of interchange
ability and check for functionality. [Different Fit Sliding, Angular, Step fit, 'T' fit, Square fit and Profile fit;
Required tolerance: ±0.04 mm, angular tolerance: 30 min.] CSC/N0304
8. Produce components involving different operations on lathe observing standard procedure and check for
accuracy. [Different Operations facing, plain turning, step turning, parting, chamfering, shoulder turn, grooving,
knurling, boring, taper turning, threading (external 'V' only)] CSC/N0110
9. Plan & perform simple repair, overhauling of different machines and check for functionality. [Different
Machines Drill Machine, Power Saw, Bench Grinder and Lathe]
10. Read and apply engineering drawing for different application in the field of work.
11. Demonstrate basic mathematical concept and principles to perform practical operations. Understand and
explain basic science in the field of study.
12. Make & assemble components of different mating surfaces as per required tolerance by different surface
finishing operations using different fastening components, tools and check functionality. [Different Mating
Surfaces - Dovetail fitting, Radius fitting, Combined fitting; Different surface finishing operations Scraping,
Lapping and Honing; Different fastening components Dowel pins, screws, bolts, keys and cotters; Different
fastening tools-hand operated & power tools, Required tolerance -±0.02mm, angular tolerance ± 10 min.]
CSC/N0304
13. Make different gauges by using standard tools & equipment and checks for specified accuracy. [Different
Gauges - Snap gauge, Gap gauge; Specified Accuracy ±0.02mm] CSC/N0304
14. Apply a range of skills to execute pipe joints, dismantle and assemble valves & fittings with pipes and test
for leakages. [Range of skills - Cutting, Threading, Flaring, Bending and Joining] CSC/N0304
15. Make drill jig & produce components on drill machine by using jigs and check for correctness. CSC/N0304
16. Plan, dismantle, repair and assemble different damaged mechanical components used for power transmission
& check functionality. [Different Damage Mechanical Components - Pulley, Gear, Keys, Jibs and Shafts.]
CSC/N0304
17. Identify, dismantle, replace and assemble different pneumatics and hydraulics components. [Different
components - Compressor, Pressure Gauge, Filter Regulator Lubricator, Valves and Actuators.]
18. Construct circuit of pneumatics and hydraulics observing standard operating procedure& safety aspect.
19. Plan & perform basic day to day preventive maintenance, repairing and check functionality. [Simple
Machines - Drill Machine, Power Saw and Lathe] CSC/N0304
20. Plan, erect simple machine and test machine tool accuracy. (Simple Machines - Drill Machine, Power Saw
and Lathe]
21. Read and apply engineering drawing for different application in the field of work.
22. Demonstrate basic mathematical concept and principles to perform practical operations. Understand and
explain basic science in the field of study.
Syllabus for Training Officer (Maths/Drawing)

2F, 3F, 1G, 2G, 3G.)(NOS: CSC/N0204)

observing standard procedure. (different types of joints Fillet (T-joint, lap & Corner), Butt (Square & V);
different position-1F, 2F, 3F, 4F, 1G, 2G, 3G, 4G) (NOS: CSC/N0204)

operation-Straight, Bevel, circular) (NOS: CSC/N0201)

pipe joints Butt, Elbow, T-joint, angle (45) joint, flange joint](NOS: CSC/N0204)

Magnetic particle test, Nick break test, Free band test, Fillet fracture test) (NOS: CSC/N0204)

cutting machine and cut ferrous & non-ferrous metals.(NOS: CSC/N0207)

14. Perform joining of different similar and dissimilar metals by brazing operation as per standard procedure.
[different similar and dissimilar metals- Copper, MS, SS] (NOS: CSC/N9410)

CSC/N9411)
16. Hard facing of alloy steel components/ MS rod by using hard facing electrode. (NOS: CSC/N9412)

explain basic science in the field of study. (NOS: CSC/N9402)

explain basic science in the field of study. (NOS: CSC/N9402)

en.title: ITI Training Officer Recruitment 2026
en.name: ITI Training Officer (various trades) Recruitment Selection Exam 2026 – Technical Education, Skill Development & Employment Dept, MP
en.body: Madhya Pradesh Employees Selection Board, Bhopal (MP Employees Selection Board, Bhopal)
en.posts: Training Officer (various trades) – total 1120 posts (Post codes 01–37: direct recruitment + backlog; e.g. Electrician 222, Mathematics/Drawing 142, Fitter 134, COPA 128, Welder 82); non-executive; pay scale 32800-103600
en.stages: Single stage written exam (one paper per trade); selection only on written-exam marks
en.negative: None – no negative marking will be applied
rules: Paper

1 paper per trade, 100 marks, 2 hours: 75 objective questions on the related trade syllabus + 25 objective questions of Class 10 level – Science and Mathematics, General Knowledge, Logical Reasoning, Basic Computer Knowledge
Marks per question
1 mark will be given for marking the correct answer to an objective question. No negative marking will be applied.
Minimum qualifying marks
In the written exam, Unreserved candidates must score at least 40% marks; OBC, SC, ST, EWS and persons with disabilities must score at least 36% marks
Language / cancelled questions
Hindi text is standard except science/technical papers (English is standard); marks of a cancelled question are given proportionately to all candidates on marks earned in the paper
Education

Trade-wise (see rulebook chapter 2). Typical: High School/11th (old course) with ITI (NCVT/SCVT) / NAC (apprenticeship) in the related trade, or 2-year course under Centre of Excellence scheme, or related engineering degree/diploma from AICTE/UGC-recognised institution
Age

18–40 yrs; 45 yrs for MP-domicile SC/ST/OBC, govt/corporation/board/autonomous employees, Nagar Sainik, PwD and women; age counted as on 01.01.2027; no age relaxation for EWS; absolute max 45 yrs; green-card holders +2, inter-caste marriage awardees & Vikram Award +5 yrs
Other
Exam only for MP domicile candidates; live registration at MP Employment Exchange mandatory; no contract-employee reservation for these 1120 posts

Unit, Fractions 1 Classification of Unit System 2 Fundamental and Derived Units F.P.S, C.G.S, M.K.S and SI

9.
